html:
October 21, 2026

New Mexico sues Epstein's accountant and attorney over alleged concealment of trafficking operation

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez announced a civil enforcement action against Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn, the former accountant and attorney for Jeffrey Epstein, accusing them of concealing and profiting from the sex trafficking operation run out of Zorro Ranch. The two men serve as executors of Epstein's estate and control a substantial share of its assets. The action seeks to direct those assets to survivors rather than to the advisors. No criminal charges have been filed in connection with the suit.

Report ties $50 million Habba legal deal to Venezuelan billionaire's pardon

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York Times reported that a Venezuelan billionaire seeking a pardon for campaign finance violations arranged a four-year, $50 million arrangement with Alina Habba, roughly $10 million a year with incentives, while she served as a senior advisor to Attorney General Pam Bondi at the Justice Department. The pardon was granted not long after the arrangement began. Habba and the Justice Department say she had no involvement in the pardon decision.

Musk ordered Starlink speed cap that degraded Ukrainian military operations

tags: war, tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

The Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials, that Elon Musk personally ordered a speed cap last week on the military version of Starlink that Ukraine relies on, leaving some Ukrainian drones unable to function. People familiar with the matter said Musk spoke with senior administration officials, including President Trump, before imposing the limit, and that the two discussed it after it became public. Trump said Monday he did not know who ordered the interruption but wanted to find out. Complaints from President Zelenskyy that the slowdown weakened Ukraine's defenses prompted an informal White House review.

Speculation grows over possible MOAB strike on Iran after Hegseth visit to Israeli air base

tags: war, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

In an October 16 Newsmax interview, Trump neither confirmed nor denied reports that he is considering using the GBU-43B Massive Ordnance Air Blast against Iran after the midterms, saying only that the weapon is not nuclear. The roughly 22,000-pound bomb is the most powerful non-nuclear weapon in the U.S. arsenal and has been used in combat once, against ISIS in 2017. Defense Secretary Hegseth met with Prime Minister Netanyahu at Uvda Air Base in Israel, a facility that hosts C-130 cargo aircraft and long-range fighter escorts, days before Israeli elections and two weeks before the U.S. midterms.

Trump envoy calls Putin a great humanitarian during Moscow visit

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas

Steve Witkoff, the administration's envoy negotiating between Russia and Ukraine, met with Vladimir Putin and publicly praised him as a great humanitarian. The remarks came as the Wall Street Journal reported Russia is stepping up destabilization operations in Europe, after a Russian spokesperson threatened Japan, and after a Russian drone strike in Ukraine killed a one-year-old girl and her mother at a park and left hundreds of thousands without power.

Governments worldwide warn of critical PHP vulnerabilities affecting most of the internet

tags: tech, surveillance
sources: @aaronparnas

The NSA and allied agencies issued an alert advising all organizations using PHP to prepare for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities, and to take systems offline if immediate patching is not feasible. Politico reported that OpenAI identified the bugs in the scripting language and that cloud security firm Wiz estimated the flaws could affect up to 70% of the internet. Similar warnings were issued in Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands, and government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline for periods during the disclosure. OpenAI described it as one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.

Trump weighs evicting the White House press corps and restoring the briefing room pool

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York Times reported that Trump has privately discussed removing the press from the White House briefing room and converting it back into a swimming pool, which exists beneath the room's floor and is currently used to run press cables. Reporters would potentially retain outdoor booths at Pebble Beach. The briefing room's location keeps journalists within reach of the Oval Office and officials for questioning.

Trump warns reporter to be careful during Oval Office exchange

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

During an Oval Office appearance, Trump told a reporter, "I don't know who the hell you are, but you better be careful," before telling the journalist to be quiet and asking whether he was a sick person. The exchange occurred as the reporter attempted to ask a question. The remarks drew comparisons to the treatment of journalists by authoritarian governments.

Trump and Vance launch $25 million program paying the public to report fraud

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews, @total.hypocrisy

Trump and Vice President JD Vance announced the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program, under which anyone whose tip submitted through fraud.gov leads to a conviction receives a 1% commission. Trump said he will act as the binding arbitrator when more than one person claims the same award and that he would be generous. Reporters were told they are also eligible to participate. The first award, $10,000, went to conservative YouTuber Nick Shirley.

Ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother roils Ohio governor's race

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Donna Arthur, the estranged mother of Ohio Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, appeared in an ad calling her daughter a liar and disputing Acton's account of growing up homeless. It is unclear who paid for the ad. Acton's brother, Philip Stearns, blamed Republican nominee Vivek Ramaswamy, saying the ad platforms a mother whose husband sexually abused Acton at age 12 and who remained married to him after Acton and her brother were removed from her custody. Ramaswamy has faced angry crowds on the campaign trail since the ad's release.

Utah County approves data center ordinance as police forcibly remove protester

tags: tech, politics, climate
sources: @carolinegleich

The Utah County Commission in Provo voted to allow data centers as a permitted use in mining, grazing and industrial zones and to create a data center overlay zone, after receiving hundreds of letters opposing the measure and weeks of public comment. More than a hundred residents packed the room, and chanting broke out after the vote. An officer identified as Phil Crawford took a protester, Aspen Azalea, to the ground, where her face struck the floor; she was the only person booked into jail and has since been released and is receiving medical care. Opponents argue the zoning change removes public accountability over how data centers are approved.

Meta removes No Kings Instagram account during national early voting push

tags: media, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Instagram took down the No Kings account on Saturday while thousands of rallies were under way urging people to vote early. Meta said its bot detection made a mistake and apologized. Organizers say early voting posts were restricted across Meta's apps. A court in Brazil this week ordered Meta to treat both presidential candidates equally after the company acknowledged technical errors had disabled some advertisements for one side. Calls have been made for Congress to demand written answers from Meta and open an investigation.

USDA to send farmers $8 billion to offset harvest diesel costs

tags: economy, politics
sources: @groundnews

Trump announced at a Kansas rally that the Department of Agriculture will launch a harvest fuel relief program providing $8 billion to farmers to offset diesel costs this harvest season. The USDA said its Farm Service Agency will distribute one-time payments using a uniform formula covering part of farmers' estimated losses for the 2026 crop year. Fuel prices have risen during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, and the announcement comes ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms, when Republicans defend narrow majorities and face competitive Senate races in farm states.

Trump ties Camp Lejeune settlements to Republican midterm wins

tags: politics, legal, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump said he will move to settle remaining Camp Lejeune water-contamination claims quickly if Republicans retain control of Congress in November, and warned there would be no money if they lose. The Justice Department reports more than $879 million in payouts so far. Existing claims remain legally active regardless of the election outcome.

Gold Star husband confronts Vance over deaths of six soldiers in Kuwait drone strike

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Joey Amor, whose wife Army Reserve Master Sgt. Nicole Amor was among six U.S. soldiers killed in an Iranian drone strike in Kuwait, confronted Vice President JD Vance at a CBS town hall over alleged failures by military leadership. Vance acknowledged mistakes involving troop locations and said he would follow up.

Trump uses term widely considered an antisemitic slur at Kansas rally

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Defending Republican Sen. Roger Marshall at a rally in Kansas, Trump said coverage of a New York Times report that Marshall sued more than 700 patients over unpaid medical bills made him out to be "some kind of a Shylock-type guy." Trump said Marshall was legally required to pursue the debts. He used the same term in a speech last year, drawing criticism from Jewish groups, and said at the time he was unaware of its antisemitic connotations.

Army investigation into fatal Black Hawk crash cites impossible arrival deadline

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Newly reported Army investigation records into the September 2025 Black Hawk crash that killed four Night Stalkers describe a deliberately impossible training arrival deadline and earlier reports of autopilot and radio problems involving the aircraft. Investigators' published findings have not established that those issues caused the crash.

Chemical explosion in Toledo prompts evacuations and shelter-in-place orders

tags: climate, health
sources: @aaronparnas

An explosion at an MC tank transport terminal in North Toledo, Ohio, around 9:30 p.m. local time released glycidyl methacrylate, prompting evacuation orders in an inner zone and shelter-in-place instructions across a three-mile radius. Residents sheltering were told to keep doors and windows shut and to turn off ventilation drawing outside air. Officials said the chemical is an irritant that can cause burning of the eyes, nose and skin along with headaches, nausea and vomiting, and reported no injuries so far. Authorities warned a further explosion is possible and are monitoring the site.

Veterans urge DeSantis to halt execution of Vietnam veteran

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

One hundred military veterans asked Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis to spare William Reaves, 77, who was scheduled for execution. Reaves was convicted of murdering sheriff's deputy Richard Raczkoski in 1986. The veterans argue that the jury that sentenced him never received critical evidence of his combat-related PTSD.

Republican congressional campaign publishes AI prompt saying the president is not popular

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

The campaign website for a Republican candidate running in Minnesota's district currently held by Angie Craig published an affordability message that still contained the AI prompt used to generate it. The prompt instructed that "the president is not popular so all messaging should be focused on local policies and needs."

Federal prosecutors charge law firm employee with stealing from disabled veterans

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Federal prosecutors accuse Darlene Toman of stealing $864,380 from 11 disabled veterans and $77,051 from an Ohio law firm that hired her in 2010 while she was serving jail time for theft. One alleged victim received a Purple Heart after being shot in Iraq. Prosecutors say much of the money funded online gambling. Toman pleaded not guilty on October 19.

Army study estimates one in four male soldiers may have low testosterone

tags: health, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A new Army study estimates that roughly 100,691 active-duty male soldiers, about one in four, could have testosterone readings below a common screening threshold, rising to 32.8% among men aged 30 and older. The Pentagon has introduced annual testosterone-deficiency screening for male troops 30 and older. A low reading alone does not establish a diagnosis.
